newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-WEBBER, GARNETT, GATLING NAMED REPLACEMENT ALL-STARS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-WEBBER, GARNETT, GATLING NAMED REPLACEMENT ALL-STARS.

text.p: Injured NBA superstars Patrick Ewing, Clyde Drexler and Shaquille O'Neal bowed out Wednesday from this weekend's All-Star game and were replaced by first-timers Chris Webber, Kevin Garnett and Chris Gatling.

Ewing, the New York Knicks' centre, has missed the last three games with a groin injury. Drexler, the Rockets' shooting guard, reinjured a hamstring against the Knicks in a Houston loss Tuesday night. O'Neal's sprained right knee kept him out of his Lakers' loss Tuesday to the Clippers.
The 20-year-old Garnett, forward for the Minnesota Timberwolves, becomes the second-youngest All-Star in NBA history, behind only Magic Johnson, who was three months younger when he played in 1980.
Garnett is averaging 16.4 points, 8.1 rebounds and 2.52 blocked shots in 42 games this season.

Garnett, who skipped college to enter the NBA Draft, was the fifth overall selection in 1995 out of Farragut Academy in Chicago. He earned second-team All-Rookie honours last season after averaging 10.4 points and 6.3 rebounds a game.

Gatling, forward for the Dallas Mavericks, leads his team in scoring (19.0 ppg) and rebounding (7.7 rpg) and is sixth in the league in field goal percentage (53.3) despite being used as a sixth man and averaging around 26 minutes a game.
Gatling, signed to a five-year contract last June, was suspended for one game last week for feuding with Dallas coach Jim Cleamons over playing time.
Ewing became the first Eastern Conference All-Star to pull out after the withdrawals of three Western Stars.
His replacement Webber, forward for the Washington Bullets, like Garnett and Gatling will be making his first All-Star appearance. He is averaging 19.8 points, 9.8 rebounds and 4.7 assists per game.
On Tuesday, Seattle SuperSonics forward Detlef Schrempf replaced Houston's Charles Barkley, the Western Conference leading vote-getter who is suffering from a sprained ankle.
Ewing was voted a starter for the East while O'Neal and Drexler were to be reserves for the West in Sunday's All-Star Game in Cleveland.
